statement: Express $3\sin\theta+4\cos\theta$ in the form $R\sin(\theta+\alpha)$ with $R>0$, and find the maximum value of $3\sin\theta+4\cos\theta$.
solution: $R=\sqrt{3^{2}+4^{2}}=5$. We need $\cos\alpha=\tfrac35$ and $\sin\alpha=\tfrac45$, so $\alpha=\arctan\tfrac43$. Thus $3\sin\theta+4\cos\theta=5\sin(\theta+\alpha)$. The maximum value of $\sin(\theta+\alpha)$ is $1$, so the maximum of the expression is $5$.
hints: Identify alpha from cos alpha=3/5, sin alpha=4/5.
The maximum of R sin(...) is R.
